angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 606,650 km at 40.34 pc = 0.2 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 76351: distance 40.34 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 40.34 +/- 0.363 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 24.6160 +/- 0.0128 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96), 1915.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 0.872 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 76351: radius 0.872 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.493 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.049) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 606,650 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5185 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 76351: effective temperature 5185 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.027) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 76351: effective temperature 5185 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.027) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 137388 (pscomppars): spectral type K2 IV, from Gray et al. 2006 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2006AJ....132..161G/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 137388: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 137388 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.19 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 137388 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.33724, from Dumusque et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A%26A...535A..55D/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 137388 (pscomppars): age 6.45 Gyr, from Dumusque et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A%26A...535A..55D/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/654/A168/tablee2 (Convective blueshifts for solar-type stars), column Prot: 40.6 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 3 catalogued periods, 3 of them within 20% of it
